what: A small example with nothing else installed
title: Getting started with saisdata
text: weo one row per country year. uses base R, works brand new R library. Net interest column; primary balance minus overall balance. Kenya’s interest bill took 5.4 percent GDP 2025, gross debt 71 percent GDP.
code: kenya <- subset(weo, code == "KEN" & year >= 2020 & year <= 2025) kenya$net_interest <- kenya$primary_balance - kenya$overall_balance  as.data.frame(kenya[, c("year", "gross_debt", "net_interest")]) #>   year gross_debt net_interest #> 1 2020     67.959        3.925 #> 2 2021     68.232        4.091 #> 3 2022     67.800        4.374 #> 4 2023     73.405        4.786 #> 5 2024     67.306        5.247 #> 6 2025     71.269        5.447

title: Getting started with saisdata
text: wb_groups joins weo code. gives typical country’s gross debt 2025 income level:
code: countries_2025 <- merge(subset(weo, year == 2025), wb_groups, by = "code")  aggregate(gross_debt ~ income_level, data = countries_2025, FUN = median) #>          income_level gross_debt #> 1         High income    55.6590 #> 2          Low income    52.2640 #> 3 Lower middle income    49.5845 #> 4 Upper middle income    54.1335

title: Getting started with saisdata
text: weo_groups keeps IMF’s layout, years across. tidyverse, two moves make tidy, one gives world’s interest bill dollars. two groups’ balances averages weighted GDP, total approximation.
code: library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(ggplot2)  bill <- weo_groups |>   select(-indicator_name, -units) |> # keep the codes, drop the long text   pivot_longer(     cols = `2001`:`2031`, # every year column     names_to = "year", # the column names become a year column     names_transform = as.integer, # "2025" becomes the number 2025     values_to = "value"   ) |>   pivot_wider(names_from = indicator, values_from = value) |> # one per indicator   mutate(     net_interest_usd_bn = (GGXONLB_NGDP - GGXCNL_NGDP) * NGDPD / 100   ) |>   summarize(net_interest_usd_bn = sum(net_interest_usd_bn), .by = year)  filter(bill, year %in% c(2001, 2025)) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>    year net_interest_usd_bn #>   <int>               <dbl> #> 1  2001                849. #> 2  2025               2371.

what: Chart it, and print the credit
title: Getting started with saisdata
text: Every chart made data carries source line. 2026 values IMF projections, chart dashes . chart uses World Bank groups, source line drops sentence.
code: labeled <- filter(bill, year %in% c(2001, 2025, 2031)) labeled$label <- format(round(labeled$net_interest_usd_bn), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)  ggplot(bill, aes(year, net_interest_usd_bn)) +   geom_line(data = filter(bill, year <= 2025), color = "#1F6F78", linewidth = 0.8) +   geom_line(     data = filter(bill, year >= 2025),     color = "#1F6F78", linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "22"   ) +   geom_point(data = labeled, color = "#1F6F78", size = 2.4) +   geom_text(     data = labeled,     aes(label = label),     hjust = c(0.5, 1.2, 0.5), # the 2025 label sits left of the line     vjust = c(-1, 0, -1),     size = 3.6,     color = "grey20"   ) +   scale_y_continuous(     limits = c(0, NA),     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14)),     labels = function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)   ) +   labs(     title = "The world's net interest bill is nearly three times its 2001 level",     subtitle = "Net interest of governments, billions of US dollars. Dashed: IMF projections",     x = NULL,     y = NULL,     caption = paste(       "Source: International Monetary Fund, World Economic Outlook Database, October 2026,",       "https://data.imf.org/en/datasets/IMF.RES:WEO.\nNet interest is the primary balance",       "minus the overall balance, calculated for this workshop."     )   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   theme(     panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),     panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),     plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8, color = "grey35"),     plot.title.position = "plot",     plot.caption.position = "plot"   )

title: World Economic Outlook, October 2026: the tidy country panel — weo
World Economic Outlook, October 2026: the tidy country panel — weo
text: tibble 6,720 rows 9 variables: code chr entity's code. country three-letter ISO code (IMF uses KOS Kosovo WBG West Bank Gaza); IMF group code starts G digit X, G110 Advanced Economies. name chr entity's name, IMF writes , "Egypt, Arab Republic ". year int year, 2000 2031. gross_debt dbl Gross debt general government, everything owes, percent GDP (IMF's GGXWDG_NGDP). primary_balance dbl primary balance: revenue minus spending, interest left sides, percent GDP (GGXONLB_NGDP). Negative means deficit. overall_balance dbl overall balance: revenue minus spending, interest included, percent GDP (GGXCNL_NGDP). Negative means deficit. gdp_usd_bn dbl GDP current prices, billions US dollars (NGDPD). latest_actual int last year actual fiscal data; later years IMF estimates projections. Missing (NA) 12 13 IMF groups. fiscal_year chr months year WEO shows fiscal numbers : "January/December" countries, others "July/June" Pakistan. Missing 12 13 IMF groups.
